subject: Post-demo: privacy & notification routing — residency decision path
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.example
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medsync.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: privacy & residency follow-up (PII, breach routing)

Hi Claire — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the privacy items you asked us to confirm: 

- Controller/Processor roles: Redwood acts as processor for feature inference (we process customer inputs on behalf of MedSync). There are a couple of callouts in the attached DPA draft where the language is flexible if you need Redwood to assume controller responsibilities for specific feature endpoints — we can discuss.
- Subprocessors: we list hosting, monitoring, and analytics subs in section 4 of the DPA. I attached a current subprocessor list and SOC2 summary.
- Breach notification: our standard timeline is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that impacts Customer Data; we’ll provide a root-cause summary and a remediation plan. Per your ask, we can add a 24-hour initial acknowledgement clause for high-priority incidents.
- Residency & retention: Hosting region options include US, EU, and APAC VPCs. Retention for inference logs (non-PII telemetry) defaults to 90 days; PII-related logs can be set per-contract.
- Logging & evidence: we can export redacted access logs and a sampling of KV-cache usage for audits (see attachment: privacy-evidence-log-samples.txt).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben will share a DPA PDF with inline comments for your legal team (attached).
2) Marissa will surface a quick cost delta for pinning an EU-only residency option for your pilot.
3) Please confirm whether you want the 24-hour ack added to the DPA and if MediSync needs Redwood to list any specific subprocessors by name in the contract.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if any of these need faster sync.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0123

--- Attachment(s): MedSync_DPA_v1.2.pdf (pdf), Redwood_SOC2_summary_2028.pdf (pdf), privacy-evidence-log-samples.txt (txt)

From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medsync.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.example
Cc: privacy@medsync.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy & residency follow-up (PII, breach routing)

Thanks Jonas — useful recap. A few clarifying Qs from our security/privacy team: 

1) For the 72h breach notification, we need clarification on the trigger point — is it when Redwood *detects* anomalous exfiltration or when Redwood has *confirmed* unauthorized access? Our legal prefers a confirmed-notify model but privacy ops wants a faster heads-up. Could you state the detection vs confirmation distinction in the language?

2) Subprocessors: please confirm whether any subcontracted MLops vendors have cross-border support (i.e., could a subprocessor process data outside the listed region temporarily for troubleshooting). We need an explicit restriction or an authorization flow.

3) Residency: for our pilot we may require EU-only hosting. What changes in logging/evidence exports if the model serving happens in an EU VPC vs Redwood-hosted multi-region?

Also, who will be the Redwood legal contact for DPA redlines (we’ll share edits via DocuSign/track changes)?

Claire
Claire Wong
Head of Platform Security, MedSync.ai
claire.wong@medsync.ai

-----
From: ben_carter@redwood.example
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medsync.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy & residency follow-up (PII, breach routing)

Hey Claire — quick answers inline to your bullets, and happy to expand on a call.

1) Detection vs confirmation: our policy is to send an initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of detection (to confirm we are investigating), and then a follow-up within 72 hours of confirmation that Customer Data was impacted. We can add both clauses to the DPA: an "Initial Acknowledgement" (24h from detection) and a "Notification of Impact" (72h from confirmation). We will record timestamps in our incident log and provide tamper-evident evidence exports to your security team.

2) Subprocessors: current MLops/hosting subprocessors are listed in the attached DPA. None automatically fail over to another region for debugging without customer consent — any cross-border troubleshooting is treated as temporary and requires documented authorization; we can add an approval flow (email + ticket) into the subprocessor section. We also keep a documented inventory and change-notice schedule (30 day notice for planned additions, immediate notice for emergency additions).

3) Residency differences: EU-only VPC means all inference execution, KV cache, and logs remain in the EU region. Exporting logs for audits will provide hashes and metadata but we can provide redacted exports if you need copies outside the EU. Functionality is identical; the main delta is a small add-on cost for dedicated regional capacity (I'll have Marissa follow-up with numbers).

Attached: updated DPA PDF with inline suggestions and our SOC2 summary.

If that works, Jonas — can you coordinate the DocuSign send and loop Redwood legal if MedSync returns redlines?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example

--- Attachment(s): MedSync_DPA_v1.2.pdf (with inline comments)

-----
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medsync.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.example
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 16 Nov 2028 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy & residency follow-up (PII, breach routing)

Hi Claire — following up with the numbers and next steps.

- EU-only residency pilot: estimated incremental monthly cost for the pilot environment is $3,200 (includes dedicated EU GPU pool + storage; contact me if you want a breakdown).
- DPA redlines: we can accept adding the 24h initial acknowledgement + 72h confirmation notification in the DPA. We will also add the subprocessor authorization flow (email + ticket) clause and the 30-day change-notice for planned additions.
- Evidence & logs: we will provide a redacted log export (CSV) and a signed hash manifest for audit requests; SOC2 report included in attachments.

Next actions: 
1) Claire — if MedSync confirms EU-only hosting for the pilot and wants the 24h clause, reply-all with confirmation and we’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope.
2) Once you confirm, Jonas will kick off the DocuSign (link will be posted and added to the HubSpot deal record).
3) If legal has specific redlines beyond the above, please upload a tracked-change PDF to the DocuSign envelope or we can review via a shared Drive link.

If you want a 30-minute call today to finalize, I’m available 4:00–5:00pm PT.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Pilot Programs) | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example
